title: Layers can hold layers
goal: Photonz keeps one flat stack of layers, so a button made of a box and a label is two separate things forever. Teach the picture that a layer can contain other layers. Nothing changes on screen yet: this is the groundwork for grouping, and after that for components.
notes: Model: add a group case to LayerContent (Layer.swift:324) carrying its children, or children on Layer, whichever keeps Codable simplest; Document.swift holds the flat array and every helper on it (layer(id:), index(of:), hitTest at :53, layerIDs(fullyInside:), addLayer, removeLayers, moveLayers, restackLayers, duplicateLayers) needs a version that reaches inside. Coordinate rule for this task: a child’s frame is relative to its parent. That is the rule an instance needs, because a component is placed at many spots and its children cannot each carry canvas coordinates. Confirm it against docs/design/next-components.md if that page has landed first. Every existing caller (renderer, measure, canvas hit testing, layers panel) assumes canvas coordinates, so ship a flattening helper that hands back canvas space layers and leave those callers on it until the renderer task lands. This is the first rung of the component ladder: groups, then the renderer, then Command G, then Make component.
acceptance: Tests come first, and they cover finding, adding, removing, reordering, duplicating, deleting and hit testing a layer that lives inside a group
A child’s position is kept against its parent, so moving the parent moves everything inside it and the same tree can sit in two places
A picture saved before this change still opens, and one containing groups survives save and open unchanged
Nothing new appears on screen: the app builds, Scripts/test.sh passes, and no group can be made from the interface yet
PhotonzCore stays pure, value typed and free of force unwraps
